lead.title: Sotheby's will sell the Blaquier-Arrieta collection in New York on 18 November, twelve works led by a Van Gogh estimated at USD 180 million
lead.standfirst: The sale is expected to test both auction records set in 2022, for Van Gogh and for Cézanne, in a single evening.
lead.body: Sotheby's has announced that it will offer twelve works from the collection of the Argentine collectors Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier and Carlos Pedro Blaquier in New York on 18 November, with a combined estimate of USD 450 million. The house describes the group as representing the development of painting in Paris from 1875 to 1905, and it is built around two pictures that each carry an estimate large enough to threaten a record. The first is Van Gogh's Châtaigniers en fleurs of 1890, painted in his final weeks at Auvers-sur-Oise and estimated at USD 180 million. It was acquired from Wildenstein & Co. in New York in 1975. The artist's auction record stands at USD 118 million, set in 2022, so the estimate alone sits well above it. The second is Cézanne's Arlequin, painted between 1888 and 1890, a portrait of the artist's son in a harlequin costume, estimated at USD 120 million. It was once owned by Lord Rothschild and later bought from the Lefevre Gallery. The Cézanne record is USD 137.8 million, also set in 2022, which means the estimate sits just under it. Beneath the two leading lots, the supporting cast is substantial. Pissarro's Place du Théâtre-Français is estimated at USD 30 million to USD 40 million, Renoir's En Canot at USD 25 million to USD 35 million, and Degas's Avant la Course at USD 20 million to USD 30 million. Collections sold whole, with a continuous history of ownership by one household, tend to attract a different class of bidder from a mixed evening sale, because the provenance is part of what is being bought. For a family that holds work of this calibre, or that is advised to bid on it, the weeks before a sale such as this are a logistics project in themselves: viewings in several cities, condition reports, loan and shipping arrangements, insurance cover from the moment a work leaves a wall, and bidding by telephone through an adviser who must be reachable at the hour the lot comes up.
lead.why: A house manager or private assistant rarely buys the painting, but is often the person who arranges the viewing, the transit, the insurance cover and the quiet room from which the principal bids.

articles.title: Family offices are flying more, and almost all of them are letting more staff on board, an Airbus Corporate Jets study finds
articles.body:
A study published by Airbus Corporate Jets this month, carried out by the independent research firm Pureprofile among 73 senior executives of family offices that together manage USD 303 billion, finds that private aircraft have become the default way these organisations move. Some 96 per cent of respondents increased their use of private jets over the past two years, and private aircraft now account for 70 per cent of all aviation travel by the family offices surveyed. The fieldwork was carried out in May 2025, so the figures describe a market a little behind the present one, and the sample is small, but the direction is consistent.

The reasons given are practical rather than aspirational. Some 89 per cent of executives say a private flight saves two to three hours per trip, and 92 per cent report at least 25 per cent greater productivity on board. The most valued benefit is the freedom to work in flight, particularly on confidential matters. Two thirds of respondents make between 25 and 50 per cent of their trips to destinations without a direct commercial service, which is one reason family offices keep opening offices abroad: nearly 70 per cent have opened one in a new jurisdiction in the past five years, and 90 per cent of those cite family members living overseas.

The finding that bears most directly on a household is about who gets to fly. Some 92 per cent of respondents already allow more staff than before to use the family's aircraft, and 97 per cent expect that access to grow over the next three years. Looking ahead, 85 per cent anticipate raising their private aviation use by between 50 and 100 per cent in the next two years, with 43 per cent expecting a rise of 50 to 75 per cent in large jet use and 55 per cent expecting the same for medium-sized jets.

An aircraft that carries the principal, the family office team and a growing share of the household staff is no longer a private space in the old sense. It becomes a workplace with a manifest, a seating plan, a catering brief and a confidentiality policy.
articles.why: When staff routinely travel on the family's aircraft, the person planning the household's movements is also managing a manifest, ground handling at several airports and the discretion of everyone on board.

articles.title: The United States has created 41 per cent of the world's new USD 30 million households since 2021, and the house at the top of the market now comes with services attached, Knight Frank finds
articles.body:
Knight Frank's Residence Report 2026, published on 9 September by Liam Bailey, its global head of research, puts a number on the shift in where the world's wealthy people are being made. Some 41 per cent of all new individuals worth USD 30 million or more between 2021 and 2026 were created in the United States, and 35 per cent of the world's ultra high net worth population now lives there. The housing market at the top has followed.

In New York, the firm counts 341 super-prime sales in the year to the first quarter of 2026, up from 281 the year before, with attention concentrated on properties above USD 20 million. One new development in the West Village, 80 Clarkson, has generated more than USD 1 billion in sales, and a new sales record for the Upper East Side was set at 1122 Madison Avenue in February. In Los Angeles, super-prime sales are rising despite the city's Measure ULA transfer tax, and Beverly Hills, which sits outside the tax's jurisdiction, remains the focal point, with the Rosewood Residences Beverly Hills and the Aman-branded One Beverly Hills setting the benchmarks.

The report adds that Miami is the world's second-largest market for branded residences, with projects from Nobu, Mandarin Oriental and Four Seasons. Developers, Knight Frank notes, now compete through distinctive design, branded living and ever more elaborate amenities, with wellness facilities close to essential.

For the people who run these homes, the amenity floor matters as much as the address. A residence with a lap pool, a wellness suite and building-run services splits the work between the building's team and the family's own staff, and someone has to draw the line between the two.
articles.why: A branded or amenity-rich residence changes the job of the house manager, who must coordinate the building's services with the family's own staff and decide what is delegated and what stays private.

articles.title: A chief of staff to a private family now commands USD 200,000 to USD 370,000, and the gap above the estate manager is widening, Achieve Hospitality's 2026 guide shows
articles.body:
Achieve Hospitality's 2026 compensation guide for American domestic and household roles, drawn from what the agency describes as active placement data and market intelligence, sets out a clear ladder at the top of the profession. A chief of staff or director of properties is placed at between USD 200,000 and USD 370,000. An estate manager earns from USD 160,000 to USD 200,000, and a house manager from USD 120,000 to USD 160,000. A personal or executive assistant covers the widest range of all, from USD 80,000 to USD 200,000.

Below the management tier, the operational roles are more tightly bunched. A head butler is placed at from USD 100,000 to USD 120,000 and a butler from USD 90,000 to USD 100,000, with a head housekeeper at from USD 100,000 to USD 120,000 and a housekeeper at from USD 80,000 to USD 100,000. A private chef is listed at from USD 120,000 to USD 200,000, a chauffeur at from USD 90,000 to USD 120,000, and a close protection officer at from USD 90,000 to USD 150,000. In childcare, a rota nanny is listed at from USD 130,000 to USD 250,000 and a governess at from USD 150,000 to USD 250,000.

The agency does not disclose the size of its sample, so the figures should be read as the asking and placement levels of one firm, not as a statistical survey. They are useful for a different reason: they show where the title above estate manager has opened up. A chief of staff to a family usually oversees several properties, the household office and sometimes the interface with the family office, and the pay band reflects a job that is closer to general management than to housekeeping.

For a manager building a career, the ladder suggests a path. Experience in running a single residence leads to a multi-property estate role, and from there to a position that sits across the household, the staff and the family's advisers.
articles.why: The top of the ladder is where a house manager's skills in budgets, vendors and people become general management, and the salary bands show what the market pays for that step.

briefs.b: Frieze London and Frieze Masters run from 14 to 18 October at The Regent's Park, with Art Basel Paris following at the Grand Palais from 21 to 25 October. It is the first Art Basel Paris under its new director, Karim Crippa, with 211 exhibitors from 41 countries.

The largest yacht at last month's Monaco Yacht Show was Nixie, a 102.4 metre Lürssen delivered in 2026, among 43 yachts delivered this year that were shown in a single harbour. New commissions typically involve waits of 2028 or later, which is why a newly delivered yacht carries a premium.

briefs.t: Miami is the second branded market
briefs.b: Knight Frank ranks Miami as the world's second-largest market for branded residences, with Nobu Residences 619 Brickell, Mandarin Oriental at Brickell Key and Four Seasons Coconut Grove among the projects. Amenities such as wellness floors are now close to a requirement for developers competing at the top.
